integrated_description: Maria should follow the parents' agreed discipline framework in all routine day-to-day care situations and refrain from unilaterally implementing her own stricter methods, instead raising concerns through a structured, evidence-based dialogue with John and Lisa—presenting specific behavioral observations and proposing incremental adjustments for mutual agreement. In immediate child-safety emergencies (e.g., dangerous aggression or imminent physical harm), Maria is permitted to take temporary, proportionate, and previously authorized safety-focused redirection actions, with prompt documentation and reporting to the parents so the long-term discipline plan remains consistent with the parental framework. If parents decline all reasonable evidence-based adjustments, Maria should document her observations, continue with the agreed approach, and—where applicable—involve a relevant agency or household manager rather than escalating discipline unilaterally.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders converged on the same core carve-out—immediate safety emergencies with prompt reporting—making full integration straightforward, while stakeholder_c's additional escalation pathway (agency/household manager when parents refuse all reasonable adjustments) was incorporated as a non-adversarial resolution mechanism that reinforces rather than undermines parental authority.
